report.summary: Chunk 5 of correctness.py: evaluate_change, verify_before_state, corpus load/save/run, seeding helpers. Docstring claims largely kept; 'never raises' broken by unguarded task['repo'].
risks: evaluate_change line ~1108 | high | evaluate_change docstring says 'never raises' but task['repo'] is an unguarded dict subscript that raises KeyError for a missing 'repo' key, contradicting the contract. | Add a try/except around task['repo'] or confirm validate_task guarantees 'repo' presence; if it does, the docstring is still misleading because validate_task runs after the docstring and the subscript is outside the try.

evaluate_change line ~1132 | medium | The docstring claims the before-state is 'never read from a stored receipt here', but the chunk does not show the internal implementation of _run_lists or judge_before_state; if those indirect helpers consult receipts, the claim is false. | Inspect _run_lists and judge_before_state in the rest of the file.

evaluate_change line ~1189 | medium | The except Exception block wraps only the before-run and patch-apply section; a KeyError from task['repo'] at line ~1132 is outside it, so the 'never raises' claim is broken as written. | Confirm validate_task runs before the subscript or add the subscript to the try.

verify_before_state line ~1215 | medium | verify_before_state docstring says 'is this task real?' and implies a candidate that fails is 'not admitted', but the function only returns a BeforeState object; the admission logic is in the caller (seeding code) and is not visible in this chunk. | Inspect the seeding caller in the rest of the file.

run_corpus line ~1286 | low | The docstring says counts are 'NEVER blended into a single score', and the returned dict has separate counts and a 'discriminates' boolean, so it is kept, but the 'discriminates' flag is derived by comparing counts to n_tasks and might be misinterpreted as a score by a downstream consumer. | Inspect callers of run_corpus for how they use 'discriminates'.

_changed_files line ~1306 | low | The parser splits on tabs and takes parts[-1] as the path; if a filename contains a tab (unlikely but possible with git quoting), the path is misparsed. Also if the diff output has a different format (e.g., no rename detection), the parser may silently return an empty list. | Add a test with a path containing a tab or unusual characters.

_blob line ~1314 | low | _blob returns None on any nonzero returncode, which could mean the blob does not exist or git failed for another reason; the caller may not distinguish 'absent' from 'unreadable'. | Inspect callers of _blob to see if they treat None as 'absent' only.

load_correctness_tasks line ~1256 | low | The function returns [] if the file does not exist, but if the file exists and contains invalid JSON, it raises json.JSONDecodeError, which is not caught. This could crash a caller that expects a graceful empty list. | Confirm whether the corpus file is expected to always be valid; if not, consider catching JSONDecodeError.

save_correctness_tasks line ~1274 | low | The function writes with a trailing newline and deterministic formatting, but there is no atomic write (write-temp-then-rename); a crash mid-write could corrupt the corpus. | Check if a crash-safe write is needed; if so, consider a temp file and os.replace.

evaluate_change line ~1165 | low | The code catches FileNotFoundError, OverlayEscape, OSError from apply_test_overlay, but not a generic Exception; other failures (e.g., a TypeError from a bad overlay) would propagate and break the 'never raises' claim. | Confirm apply_test_overlay only raises those exceptions.

evaluate_change line ~1170 | low | The code uses _check_selection to detect moved nodes; if _check_selection itself has a bug, the evaluation may incorrectly report a moved node. | Add tests for _check_selection.

evaluate_change line ~1195 | low | The after-state run is inside the same try/except as the before-state, so any exception during the after-run is caught and reported as 'could_not_run', which is appropriate, but the docstring says 'never raises' which is kept only if the exception is caught. Since the except is broad, the claim is kept for that section. | No action needed.

CORPUS_NOTE line ~1262 | low | The note claims 'every task's lists were MEASURED... never taken from the diff on trust' and 'the gate refuses a task whose lists no longer digest to it'. This chunk does not show the measurement or the gate's refusal logic; it is uncheckable. | Inspect the seeding code and the gate in the rest of the file.

_changed_files line ~1306 | low | The function returns [] on any nonzero returncode, which could mask a git error (e.g., bad SHA) as 'no changes'. This could cause a task to be seeded with empty lists. | Consider distinguishing 'no changes' from 'git error' by checking stderr or raising on unexpected returncode.

handoff.purpose: Defines evaluate_change, verify_before_state, corpus load/save/run, and seeding helpers (_changed_files, _blob, _test_functions).

symbols.name: evaluate_change
symbols.note: Evaluates one change against one task. Returns CorrectnessResult, never raises (claimed). Freezes selection, runs before/after in a disposable worktree.

symbols.name: verify_before_state
symbols.note: Measures only the before-state of a task; returns BeforeState. Used for seeding corpus.

symbols.name: _slug
symbols.note: Sanitizes a string to a slug for worktree labels.

symbols.name: load_correctness_tasks
symbols.note: Reads corpus JSON from path or DEFAULT_CORPUS_PATH, returns sorted list of tasks.

symbols.name: CORPUS_NOTE
symbols.note: String describing corpus provenance and verification commands.

symbols.name: save_correctness_tasks
symbols.note: Overwrites corpus file with deterministic formatting and trailing newline.

symbols.name: run_corpus
symbols.note: Evaluates every task against its own reference patch; returns counts per outcome and discriminates flag.

symbols.name: _changed_files
symbols.note: Returns list of (status, path) from git diff --name-status -r --no-renames.

symbols.name: _blob
symbols.note: Returns file content at rev:rel or None if git show fails.

symbols.name: _test_functions
symbols.note: Starts at line 1318; not fully shown in this chunk.

claims.text: Evaluate one change against one task. Returns; never raises.
claims.why: The docstring claims the function never raises, but task['repo'] on line ~1132 is an unguarded dict subscript that raises KeyError if 'repo' is missing. This is outside the try/except block that starts later, so the exception propagates.

claims.text: The whole measurement happens in ONE disposable worktree, in this order: FREEZE the selection -> checkout base -> overlay tests -> RUN BEFORE -> judge the TASK -> apply the change -> RUN AFTER -> judge the CHANGE
claims.why: The code follows this order: freeze_selection, disposable_worktree, apply_test_overlay, _run_lists (before), judge_before_state, apply_patch, _run_lists (after), judge_after_state.

claims.text: The selection is frozen FIRST, before the worktree exists and long before any candidate bytes are applied, and the after-state is run against that same frozen object -- so the thing being measured cannot be influenced by the thing being measured. The frozen declaration and its digest travel on the result.
claims.why: freeze_selection is called before disposable_worktree and before any patch application; the same selection object is passed to both _run_lists calls and to finish(). The digest travels on CorrectnessResult via selection.

claims.text: The before-state is measured every time, in the same tree the after-state is measured in. It is never read from a stored receipt here, because a receipt is a claim about a tree that may no longer exist -- the same doctrine spine.bootstrap applies to its discrimination receipt.
claims.why: The chunk shows that before-state is measured via _run_lists and judge_before_state in the same worktree, but it does not show the implementation of _run_lists or judge_before_state. If those helpers read receipts, the claim would be broken; this chunk cannot confirm that.

claims.text: use_reference evaluates the task's OWN fix commit (reference_revision) instead of a candidate patch. That is how a corpus task is validated: a task whose own reference patch does not produce fixed is not a task.
claims.why: When use_reference is true, the code calls reference_patch(root, base, task['reference_revision'], ...) and applies that instead of patch_bytes. The docstring's claim about corpus validation is not directly testable here but the mechanism is present.

claims.text: Measure ONLY the before-state of task: is this task real? Used when seeding a corpus. A candidate task that does not survive this is reported, with its reasons, and not admitted -- which is the measurement that says how much a corpus is worth.
claims.why: The function returns a BeforeState with reasons and flags, but the admission logic (whether a failed candidate is 'not admitted') is in the caller (seeding code) not shown in this chunk. The function itself does not admit or reject.

claims.text: Read the corpus, or [] if it does not exist yet. Sorted by id.
claims.why: The function checks os.path.exists(p) and returns [] if not; otherwise it loads JSON and returns sorted tasks by id.

claims.text: Overwrite the corpus. Deterministic formatting, same contract as harness.write_baseline / mint.save_minted_tasks.
claims.why: The function sorts tasks by id, writes with indent=2, sort_keys=True, and adds a trailing newline, which is deterministic. The contract with harness/mint is not verifiable here but the formatting is as described.

claims.text: Evaluate every task against its OWN reference patch. The corpus's own gate.
claims.why: The code calls evaluate_change(task, use_reference=True, ...) for each task, which uses the task's reference_revision.

claims.text: Counts are reported per outcome and NEVER blended into a single 'score' -- task_invalid and could_not_run in particular are not failures of the change, and folding them into one number would hide exactly the distinction this module was built for.
claims.why: The function returns a dict with separate counts per outcome and a 'discriminates' boolean, not a single blended score.

claims.text: Records every node that did not survive, and why. Verify with 'python -m daedalus.eval.correctness --verify'; re-measure every task against its own reference fix with '--run'. These tasks are NOT in harness.all_tasks(): slice recall cannot grade them (they have no must_include and would score a vacuous 1.0), and the harness refuses them.
claims.why: The note makes claims about dropped_candidates (not visible in this chunk), CLI commands (not visible), and harness behavior (not visible). The chunk only defines the constant; the claims reach beyond.

observations.what: evaluate_change docstring says 'never raises' but task['repo'] is an unguarded dict subscript that can raise KeyError, outside the try/except block.
The claim that before-state is never read from a stored receipt depends on _run_lists and judge_before_state, which are not visible in this chunk.
verify_before_state returns a BeforeState but the 'not admitted' behavior is in the caller, not visible here.
load_correctness_tasks returns [] only if the file does not exist; if the file exists but is invalid JSON, it raises JSONDecodeError uncaught.
save_correctness_tasks writes non-atomically; a crash mid-write could corrupt the corpus.
_changed_files parses diff output by splitting on tabs; filenames with tabs (though rare) would be misparsed, and any nonzero returncode silently yields [].
_blob returns None on any nonzero returncode, conflating 'absent' with 'git error'.
CORPUS_NOTE makes claims about measurement and gate refusal that are not verifiable in this chunk.
